key_insight: Choosing the molecular enantiomer reverses polarization and the persistent spin texture in polar chiral two-dimensional lead-halide perovskites.
engineering_relevance: These materials offer a route to molecularly selected spin orientation for nanoscale spintronic devices, rather than a demonstrated improvement in solar-cell efficiency.
method: Derived symmetry-allowed spin–orbit interactions for polar chiral perovskites.
Calculated first-principles spin textures for ten compounds, their mirror enantiomers and four halide-substituted analogues.
Compared 34 two-band k·p models using spin-direction agreement rather than band energies.
evidence_signal: For strongly polar compounds, the persistent-term conduction-band model achieved spin agreement ≥0.98 versus 0.20 for the best Rashba or Dresselhaus model, with predicted spin-helix wavelengths of 3.4–8.2 nm.
watch_item: The computational predictions still require experimental validation of persistent spin textures and their robustness under device operating conditions.
paper_title: Polarization-locked chiral persistent spin textures in two-dimensional lead-halide perovskites
